title: Overpass error-remark guard searches XML token '<remark>' and can never match the [out:json] responses the tool requests
evidence:
# Overpass reports errors as 200 JSON with a <remark> element
            text = body.decode("utf-8")
            if "<remark>" in text:
                raise RuntimeError(f"Overpass remark: {text[:500]}")
detail: Both pinned queries use [out:json] (GEOM_QUERY/BUILDING_QUERY start with it); JSON errors carry a "remark" key, never '<remark>'. A 200 timed-out response with partial elements is cached as valid and silently baked — mirror failover and the RuntimeError path never fire.
recommended_fix: Detect the JSON form: parse or regex the body for '"remark"' and refuse to cache (raise, so the except clause tries the next mirror) when present.

title: Fetch failover except-tuple misses gzip/decode errors, aborting the 3-mirror loop with a traceback
detail: gzip.BadGzipFile/EOFError, UnicodeDecodeError (e.g. a 'GZIP' header value skips decompression since the header match is case-sensitive), or http.client.IncompleteRead escape the except tuple and crash instead of trying the remaining mirrors.
recommended_fix: Broaden the except to OSError and ValueError (BadGzipFile and UnicodeDecodeError are subclasses), and match Content-Encoding case-insensitively.

title: --verify without a populated cache dies with a raw FileNotFoundError traceback
detail: The --verify branch returns before any fetch, and load_raw/load_raw_set have no missing-file handling; on a fresh clone (.osm-cache/ is gitignored and absent) verify() crashes with FileNotFoundError instead of a clean message. Same for a missing out_path.
recommended_fix: In verify()/load_raw_set, catch FileNotFoundError and exit with a hint to run --fetch (or fetch first) before verifying.

title: Non-atomic cache write plus existence-only cache-hit check poisons the cache on interruption
evidence:
if os.path.exists(path):
            print(f"[fetch] cache hit: {path}")
            continue
        _post_one(q, path)
...
            with open(path, "w") as f:
                f.write(text)
detail: A Ctrl-C or crash during f.write leaves a truncated JSON file; cache-first only checks os.path.exists, so every later run hits the poisoned file and dies in json.load until it is deleted by hand.
recommended_fix: Write to a temp path and os.replace() into place, so the cache only ever contains complete responses.

title: Multi-member relations are flattened into one concatenated LineString, so multi-ring water bodies are silently dropped
detail: GEOM_QUERY explicitly fetches relation[natural=water]/[waterway=riverbank], but outer+inner (or multi-part) members get joined with straight jump chords into one self-intersecting ring; Polygon(...).is_valid is then False and the whole body is discarded — no member-role handling exists.
recommended_fix: Assemble member rings per role (outer rings as polygons, inner as holes; Polygonize each member separately) instead of concatenating all member points.

title: MIN_AREA comments overstate the effective noise-floor sizes by 3-9x at the baked scale
detail: With the baked scale_tiles_per_m 0.0013971214 (1 tile = 715.76 m), 0.01 tiles² is 5,123 m² ≈ 72x72 m — not ~220x220 m (that is 0.0945 tiles²); park 0.1 tiles² is ~7 football fields, so 2-field parks the comment claims to keep are actually dropped.
recommended_fix: Either correct the comments to the real sizes (72 m / ~7 fields) or retune the values to the documented intent (~0.095 water, ~0.028 park).

title: fetched_utc is baked from cache-file mtimes, so byte-identical re-bakes break across machines/re-fetches
detail: Re-fetching identical raw data (or copying/cloning the cache) changes st_mtime, changing the asset's fetched_utc field and its bytes; the committed dublin.json is not byte-reproducible elsewhere despite the raw_sha256 pin — verify only compares a local re-bake.
recommended_fix: Derive fetched_utc from the Overpass 'osm3s.timestamp_osm_base' field inside the cached response instead of filesystem mtimes.
